fact: Lei 10/2024, published in the Boletim da Republica on 7 June 2024, gives persons with disabilities a right of access to information and communication technologies and systems (Article 16) and says public service entities should provide service information in accessible formats, with sign-language training for State communicators (Article 17).

The ITU-EU VaMoz Digital project, supporting Mozambique's government 2023-2027, completed a digital accessibility assessment with special focus on persons with disabilities and ran digital accessibility awareness and training (5 webinars, 4 workshops, 3 focus groups) reaching 320+ stakeholders, according to ITU.

Forbes África Lusófona reports the Ministry of Communications and Digital Transformation is leading the drafting of a National Digital Inclusion Strategy with a five-year action plan, prioritising people with disabilities among other groups.

INTIC's Onelio Zavala said Mozambique has no national digital accessibility standard based on WCAG yet, and INTIC plans to develop national digital accessibility norms aligned with international standards.
